notes_for_editor:
Maryland Point: moderate-to-rich record. Sources: the USLHS roster (46 lines), LighthouseFriends (facts only), the Board's reports in the local corpus (1892-1897), the Commissioner's report for 1921 in the corpus, the Lighthouse Service Bulletins for 1918 and 1926 and the 1918-1923 index, the Evening Star for 8 February 1920 and 1 September 1954, the Lighthouse Directory, and three USLHS person records.
Disagreements stated: the date of the 1920 abandonment (LighthouseFriends 5 February; the Star's dispatch dated 7 February says 'yesterday', 6 February); the length of Loch W. Humphreys' stint here (roster 1905-1909; his person record's entries run 1905 to 1911 and then Piney Point, which the story does not state as a date); the wooden house's end (Directory and LighthouseFriends 1963; the record says 'standing').
Corrections proposed for the record: status 'inactive' (the Directory lists the current skeletal light as active); the structure 'tower, screwpile, wood, built 1892, 12.8 m, standing' should read removed 1963 (LighthouseFriends and the Directory) with the present steel skeletal tower on the original foundation.
Place: the record and USLHS name it 'Riverside, MD'; the Directory and LighthouseFriends put it midstream between Wellington Beach (MD) and Fairview Beach (VA). The story follows the Directory and LighthouseFriends.
OCR: the 1918 Bulletin splits names and words ('Mary land Point Llgbt'), so the quotations use the clean fragments only; the 1893 report's 'wrougbt-iron' is quoted as OCR'd. The 1926 Bulletin's name 'J. E. Morgan' is read from a split line; the roster and the archive's person record agree on John E. Morgan.
Star quotations: the 1920 OCR reads 'Navy tug Howard P. Green' across a line break; the quote is taken from the clean line. The 1954 Star names the keeper by OCR as 'Keeper George W. Austin'; the roster gives the same name and dates.
Unused: the 1920 Bulletin index entry 'Maryland Point light station keepers seek safety' (page 118 of the 1918-1923 index) could not be matched to the text, so it is not used; a Board statement about the Potomac lights (the Commissioner's 1915-1922 reports) is not used either.
Not searched: photos; keepers' families; the Piney Point link is recorded on the person archive, not in Fresnel's Piney Point story.
Fact-check 2026-10-28: the 1896 riprap and the 1893 first light are dated to their fiscal-year reports; the 1921 Commissioner entry is dated to the fiscal year ended June 30, 1921 (the corpus label); Andrew J. Jarvis's 1903 stint (roster line) is now in the story; the 1920 dispatch's 'yesterday' is compared with LighthouseFriends' 5 February.
